verses.1: Now while Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came up to them,
verses.2: agitated because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead,
verses.3: and they laid hands on them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
verses.4: But many of those who had heard the message believed, and the number of men came to be about five thousand.
verses.5: On the next day their rulers, elders, and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem,
verses.6: (and Annas the high priest and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and all who were of the high priestly family),
verses.7: and standing them in the middle, they asked, "In what power or in what name have you done this?"
verses.8: Then Peter filled with the Holy Spirit said to them, "You leaders of the people and elders,
verses.9: if we are being examined today concerning a good deed done to a crippled man, in whom this one was healed,
verses.10: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus the Messiah of Nazareth, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, in this name this man stands before you healthy.
verses.11: This is the stone that was rejected by you, the builders, which has become the cornerstone.
verses.12: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among people by which we must be saved."
verses.13: Observing the boldness of Peter and John and perceiving that they were uneducated and ordinary men, they were amazed, and they recognized that they had been with Jesus,
verses.14: and looking at the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against it.
verses.15: So they commanded them to go out of the council and began to consult with one another,
verses.16: saying, "What should we do to these men? For indeed a clear sign has come to be through them in all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it;
verses.17: but so that it might not spread further among the people, let us warn them not to speak to anyone in this name."
verses.18: And calling them, they commanded them not to speak at all, nor to teach in the name of Jesus.
verses.19: But Peter and John answered them, "Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, you decide,
verses.20: for we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard."
verses.21: And those who had threatened them released them, finding nothing to punish them with, because of the people, for all were glorifying God for what had happened;
verses.22: for the man on whom this sign of healing had come was more than forty years old.
verses.23: Released, they went to their own company and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.
verses.24: Now when they heard this, they raised a united voice to God and said, "Lord, you are the one who made the heavens and the earth and the sea, and all that is in them,
verses.25: the one who through the Holy Spirit spoke by the mouth of our father David, your servant, saying, 'Why did the Gentiles rage, and the peoples imagine emptiness?'
verses.26: 'The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against his Messiah.'"
verses.27: For indeed, they have conspired in this city against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed, Herod and Pontius Pilate, along with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel,
verses.28: to do whatever your hand and your plan had determined beforehand to happen.
verses.29: And now, Lord, look at their threats, and grant to your servants to speak your word with all boldness,
verses.30: while you stretch out your hand to heal, and signs and wonders are done through the name of your holy servant Jesus."
verses.31: And when they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness.
verses.32: Now the whole community of those who believed was one in heart and soul, and no one claimed that anything of what they possessed was their own, but all things were common to them.
verses.33: And with great power the apostles gave their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon all of them.
verses.34: For indeed, there was no one among them who was in need, for those who owned lands or houses sold them and brought the proceeds of what was sold,
verses.35: and laid them at the feet of the apostles. Distribution was made to each person as anyone had need.
verses.36: Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles, which is interpreted "Son of encouragement," a Levite from Cyprus,
verses.37: having a field, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the feet of the apostles.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: "in no one else" is a translation of "ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ," which emphasizes the exclusivity of salvation in Jesus.
- v. 19: "we cannot stop speaking" reflects the Greek "οὐ δυνάμεθα ... μὴ λαλεῖν," capturing the impossibility of remaining silent.
- v. 27: "the kings of the earth took their stand" translates the poetic reference to Psalm 2:2, which is echoed in Acts.
- v. 34-35: The communal sharing described here aligns with the Greek terms "οὐδὲ ἐνδεής ... ἀλλʼ ἦν αὐτοῖς πάντα κοινά," highlighting a radical economic unity in the early church.
